title: Patch: the AI's tests run on an optimised AI, as the engine's and the cards' already do
thread:
**Issue #1643 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1643: Patch: the AI's tests run on an optimised AI, as the engine's and the cards' already do
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The tests that play practice-AI games take minutes on every pull request that touches the AI. Most of that time goes to running the AI's search code without compiler optimisation: the test build optimises the rules and the cards, but not the AI. Once this is built, and only if the measurement bears it out, the AI's test groups and the other groups that play AI games finish sooner with exactly the same results. The maintainer and the bot notice shorter CI waits; nobody playing notices.

## Why
- `Cargo.toml:58-83` sets `opt-level = 2` under `[profile.test.package.*]` for `jackioh-engine`, `jackioh-cards`, `jackioh-luau`, `mlua-sys`, `mlua`, `serde_json` and `indexmap`, because unoptimised golden replays "take hours" (its comment).
- `jackioh-ai` is not on that list and never was: `git log -S"profile.test.package.jackioh-ai" -- Cargo.toml` finds nothing.
- The CI workflow says the AI's tests "take minutes to play their games rather than to compile". The `ai` and `ai slow` groups were split in #878 (`5ba7d50c4`) to keep each under the five-minute budget, and #1608 (a job over seven minutes) is open.
- Other groups play AI seats per pull request too: the handicapped fuzz wave in `tools, wasm` (`crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs:3656`, Medium and Hard seats), and the server's ladder-bot tests.
- The AI's search is budgeted in nodes (`AI_BUDGET`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:35`), so optimisation changes its speed, not its decisions. Rust does no fast-math, so results and hashes stay the same.

## Proposal
Measure first. Time the compile (`--no-run`) and the run separately, from a cold `target/`, before and after:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai_slow`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server`

The "after" needs no edit: add `--config 'profile.test.package.jackioh-ai.opt-level=2'` to each command. Only if the AI groups' compile plus run gets shorter, add `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai] opt-level = 2` beside the others in `Cargo.toml`, with a comment carrying the numbers. Debug assertions and overflow checks stay on, as they do for the engine.

## Where it lands
- `Cargo.toml` (the test profile). Nothing else.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The pull request shows before/after compile and run times for the three commands, measured the same way on the same machine.
- [ ] It changes `Cargo.toml` only if the `ai` and `ai slow` commands' compile plus run is shorter after. Otherwise nothing ships, and the numbers are reported on the issue.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai --test ai_slow`, the golden replay and `cargo jackioh gate` pass with no test changed.

## Size and risks
Two lines and a comment; the work is the measurement. The risk is that the AI's source and its integration tests, which then also build at opt-level 2, cost more to compile than the faster games save. That is why it ships only on numbers. The first CI run after it rebuilds the AI groups' cache cold.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/39804226168)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Time the issue's three commands from a cold target dir, compile (`--no-run`) and run separately, before and after `--config 'profile.test.package.jackioh-ai.opt-level=2'`. Add `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai] opt-level = 2` to `Cargo.toml`, with a comment carrying the numbers, **only if** compile plus run gets shorter for both the `ai` and the `ai slow` command. Otherwise nothing ships and the numbers go on the issue.

**The planner already measured once, and nothing should ship.** On a fresh 4-core runner, with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` (the settings CI uses, `ci.yml:101`), all runs exited 0. Times are in seconds, compile + run = total:

| command | opt-level 0 (before) | opt-level 2 (after) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai` | 120.8 + 52.1 = **172.9** | 177.4 + 26.1 = **203.5** | +30.6 |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai_slow` | 113.0 + 34.5 = **147.5** | 135.5 + 25.8 = **161.3** | +13.8 |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-server` | 234.3 + 101.4 = **335.7** | 245.9 + 85.4 = **331.3** | −4.4 |

For information only, opt-level 1 was also slower: `ai` 151.8 + 28.6 = 180.4, `ai slow` 127.3 + 26.7 = 154.0. The games run faster, but compiling the AI crate's own lib and test binaries at opt-level 2 costs more than that saves.

The builder measures again (a second sample, seen with its own eyes) and applies the rule in step 5.

## Files to touch

| File | new/change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml` | change, **ship path only** | A new `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]` block with `opt-level = 2` and a comment carrying the numbers. It goes right after `[profile.test.package.indexmap]` (lines 82–83), before the `# The server and the WASM module…` comment (line 85). |

On the expected path (nothing ships) **no tracked file changes**.

Do not touch:
- `.github/` (ci.yml's comments at lines 213–216 about the AI's tests stay as they are).
- `crates/ai/`, any test, any README or doc, `spec/`, `BUILD.md` and `Cargo.lock`.

No spec section or ruling governs this. It is build configuration, not a rule, so there is no new ruling, no patch fragment (`classify` files `Cargo.toml` under `Area::Internal`, so its kind is internal with no tier) and no `spec check` change.

## Steps

1. **Check the machine.**
   - Run `git status --porcelain`; it must be empty.
   - Run `nproc` and `uptime`, and note both for the report.
   - While measuring, do not run any other cargo command, subagent or build. Anything else on the CPU skews the times.

2. **Write the timing script.** It goes outside the worktree, at `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/jackioh-1643/measure.sh`; run `mkdir -p "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/jackioh-1643"` first. Copy it exactly:

   ```bash
   #!/usr/bin/env bash
   # #1643: times `cargo test <args> --no-run` (the compile), then `cargo test <args>` (the run), from
   # an empty target dir, as CI builds: no incremental cache, no debuginfo in the test profile.
   # usage: measure.sh <label> <before|after> <cargo test args...>
   set -u
   label=$1; variant=$2; shift 2
   cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1
   out=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/jackioh-1643
   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0
   dir=$out/target-$label-$variant
   rm -rf "$dir"
   config=()
   if [ "$variant" = after ]; then
     config=(--config 'profile.test.package.jackioh-ai.opt-level=2')
   fi
   log=$out/$label-$variant.log
   t0=$EPOCHREALTIME
   CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$dir cargo test "${config[@]}" "$@" --no-run >"$log" 2>&1
   c=$?
   t1=$EPOCHREALTIME
   CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$dir cargo test "${config[@]}" "$@" >>"$log" 2>&1
   r=$?
   t2=$EPOCHREALTIME
   compile=$(awk -v a="$t0" -v b="$t1" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", b - a }')
   run=$(awk -v a="$t1" -v b="$t2" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", b - a }')
   echo "$label $variant compile=${compile}s (exit $c) run=${run}s (exit $r)" | tee -a "$out/results.txt"
   rm -rf "$dir"
   ```

3. **Run the six measurements** from the worktree root, in this order. Use one Bash call with `run_in_background: true` and `timeout: 7200000`, then wait for its notification; the planner's run of all six took about 23 minutes.

   ```bash
   M="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/jackioh-1643"; : > "$M/results.txt"
   bash "$M/measure.sh" ai before -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai
   bash "$M/measure.sh" ai after -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai
   bash "$M/measure.sh" ai_slow before -p jackioh-ai --test ai_slow
   bash "$M/measure.sh" ai_slow after -p jackioh-ai --test ai_slow
   bash "$M/measure.sh" server before -p jackioh-server
   bash "$M/measure.sh" server after -p jackioh-server
   echo ALL DONE >> "$M/results.txt"
   ```

4. **Read `$M/results.txt`.**
   - Every line must show `exit 0` twice.
   - If an `after` run fails where its `before` passed, the AI's results depend on optimisation, which they must not. Do not ship. Stop `blocked` and name the failing test from `$M/<label>-after.log`.
   - If a `before` run fails, stop `blocked` with the log's failure.
   - Then run `git status --porcelain`. It must still be empty: the server's `export_config` test rewrites `serverConfig.ts` to the same bytes.

5. **Decide.** For each of `ai` and `ai_slow`, the total is compile + run. Add your totals to the planner's from the Goal table:
   - `ai`: (172.9 + your before) against (203.5 + your after).
   - `ai_slow`: (147.5 + your before) against (161.3 + your after).

   **Ship only if both after sums are below their before sums.** The server's numbers are reported but decide nothing, as the issue says.

6. **A. Nothing ships (expected).** Change no file. Your final message's first line is:

   ```

   ```

The planner's: `ai` 120.8+52.1=172.9 → 177.4+26.1=203.5; `ai slow` 113.0+34.5=147.5 → 135.5+25.8=161.3; `server` 234.3+101.4=335.7 → 245.9+85.4=331.3. At opt-level 1 (planner): `ai` 180.4, `ai slow` 154.0. The faster games do not pay for compiling the AI crate's own units at opt-level 2, so by the issue nothing ships and Cargo.toml is unchanged. Close #1643 as not planned, or name another setting to measure.

   After that line, put the same numbers in a Markdown table, followed by the two decisions under **Open questions**.

7. **B. Ship (only if step 5 says so).** In `Cargo.toml`, after line 83 (`opt-level = 2` of `[profile.test.package.indexmap]`), insert one blank line and then the block below. Put each measured total (both samples, before → after) where `<…>` stands, and wrap the comment at 100 columns like its neighbours. Change nothing else.

   ```toml
   # The AI, whose tests play whole games through its search (`ai`, `ai slow`, the server's ladder
   # bots). Its search is budgeted in nodes (`AI_BUDGET`), so its speed never changes a decision.
   # Timed from an empty target/ as CI builds (#1643), compile + run at 0 and at 2: `-p jackioh-ai
   # --lib --test ai` <…> s and <…> s, `--test ai_slow` <…> s and <…> s, `-p jackioh-server` <…> s
   # and <…> s.
   [profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]
   opt-level = 2
   ```

   Run the commands under **Tests**. Then write the final message:
   - First line: `<!-- bot: {"status": "done", "title": "Patch: the AI's tests run on an optimised AI, as the engine's and the cards' already do"} -->`.
   - Then the before/after table for all three commands (both samples), the commands you ran with what they printed, and the decisions below.

## Tests

No test is added or changed; the issue forbids it. On the nothing-ships path, the six measurements are the evidence. On the ship path, run these and report what each prints:

- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai --test ai_slow`: all pass.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test golden`: the golden replay passes. The engine does not depend on the AI, so it cannot change, but the issue lists it.
- `cargo jackioh gate`: passes. It is a release build, which the test profile does not reach.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: kind internal, no problems.
- `cargo fmt --check`.
- `git diff --stat`: shows `Cargo.toml` only, one block added.

## Done when

- [ ] All six measurements ran on one machine, nothing else building, and every one exited 0.
- [ ] The decision follows step 5's sum rule.
- [ ] Nothing-ships path: `git status --porcelain` is empty, and the final message is `blocked` with every number in `question`.
- [ ] Ship path: `Cargo.toml` alone changed, with the comment carrying the numbers, and every command under **Tests** passed.
- [ ] Ship path: the harness checks pass (rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests). No check is called green before it has run (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
- [ ] Every target dir under `$M` has been removed (the script does it); only logs remain.

## Risks

- **Noise.** A single cold sample per row is noisy, which is why step 5 sums two samples. The planner's gaps are +18% (`ai`) and +9% (`ai slow`); a lone noisy run should not flip them.
- **Determinism and replay.** Rust does no fast-math, and setting only `opt-level` keeps debug assertions and overflow checks on, as for the engine. The planner's opt-level 2 runs passed the very same tests. Step 4 stops the build if they ever do not.
- **CI on the ship path.** A change to the workspace `Cargo.toml` runs every CI job (`scripts/ci-scope.sh:194`), and the first run rebuilds the AI groups' cache cold. Expected, and stated in the issue.
- **Disk.** Each cold target dir holds a few GB; the script deletes each one when its measurement is done.
- **The measurement machine.** If `uptime`'s load average is above `nproc` before you start, say so in the report: the numbers are then less reliable.

## Open questions

- **Decision taken in this plan, to record in the report:** two samples are summed (step 5). Rejected: letting the builder's single run decide alone, which one noisy cold build could flip against the planner's result.
- **Decision taken in this plan:** both `ai` and `ai slow` must each be shorter. Rejected: comparing the two commands' combined total, because CI runs them as separate jobs, each with its own five-minute budget.
- **For a person, if nothing ships:** close #1643 as not planned, or ask for another setting to be measured. Opt-level 1 was measured above and was also slower.
````
